直列半音豎琴屬弦鳴樂器，其發聲結構將一個八度內十二個半音集中於同一排弦，而非分置: The inline chromatic harp is a chordophone. Its sounding structure gathers the twelve semitones of an octave into one row of strings instead of splitting them across two rows or crossed rows. The known fifty-four-string model covers four octaves and a fourth, so the pitch layout is more concentrated than in the multi-row layouts of the same family. That structure allows glissandos only in semitones, a playing limitation that clearly sets it apart from its relatives. 直列半音豎琴的單排形式至少已有百餘年生產紀錄；1902年，漢諾威（德國）的Kar: The single-row form of the inline chromatic harp has been in production for at least a hundred years; in 1902 Karel Weigel of Hanover (Germany) took out a patent on an inline chromatic harp and built at least one with 54 strings and a range of four and a quarter octaves, now in the Deutsches Museum in Munich. At least one example with two parallel chromatic rows has also been produced.
